newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge freezes Menem labor reform decrees.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge freezes Menem labor reform decrees.

text.p: President Carlos Menem's attempt to reform Argentina's labor laws by decree, recently declared unconstitutional by one judge, suffered another blow Monday when another labor judge ruled they must be frozen.

Labor Judge Ines Gassibe, acting on a petition by the main CGT trade union federation, ruled that the government "will refrain from putting the decrees into effect" pending a full explanation of the decree decision in late December.

Menem, who believes more flexible labor laws would help fight high unemployment, resorted to decrees in the face of opposition in Congress and a breakdown in negotiations with unions, who fear their power is under threat. The CGT staged a 24-hour general strike on December 26, its third in the year.

The Peronist government had been working on another batch of decrees to follow up the first three, which allow workers to choose their union health plan, let smaller firms bypass national unions in collective pay talks and let firms appeal to the government if they wanted to negotiate with unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.
But the project received a setback 10 days ago when Labor Judge Julio Garcia Martinez ruled they were unconstitutional.
Menem's ministers slammed that ruling as "more political and ideological than judicial" and pledged to annul it and have Judge Garcia Martinez impeached.
However the CGT moved swiftly to follow up that ruling by appealing last Friday for the decrees to be suspended while their status is resolved.
CGT press chief Carlos West Ocampo told reporters Monday that the latest ruling might facilitate dialogue.
"It's not the same to sit down to negotiate with decrees already in effect and threats of new ones as it is to start a dialogue with the decrees suspended," said West Ocampo.

The debate has whipped up a summer storm in Argentine politics, with 77-year-old Judge Garcia Martinez -- himself a Peronist -- responding to the government's threat to have him impeached: "It's the first time in Argentine court history, from 1853 to the present day, that they have tried to throw out a judge for defending the constitution."
